nodes.label: Painful, crusted erythematous plaque on the right chest for 2 weeks
Patient is a woman in her 50s
Physical examination demonstrated a large, crusted, erythematous plaque on the right chest
Patient was taking prednisone 10 mg daily and had not used any topical medications

Previous treatments included methotrexate, mycophenolate mofetil, cyclosporine, glycopyrrolate, oral antibiotics, topical corticosteroids, topical calcineurin inhibitors, and topical antibiotics, all of which were unsuccessful
Prior skin biopsy was performed, but histopathologic and immunohistochemical details are unavailable
Radiologist recommends TCR rearrangement studies to evaluate possible T-cell lymphoma
The lesion may be a cutaneous T-cell lymphoma (e.g., mycosis fungoides)
Pathologist analysis reports that the original biopsy report and molecular results could not be retrieved despite repeated searches
Radiologist analysis states histopathology and immunohistochemistry are still required for confirmation
Both expert analyses rank cutaneous neoplasm/lymphoma as the leading hypothesis
Both expert analyses consider infection and inflammatory dermatosis less likely given treatment failures
Mycosis fungoides, a cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
Cutaneous metastasis from an occult malignancy
Laboratory and imaging staging information has not been obtained
Pathologist analysis states key histological and molecular evidence is insufficient and cannot completely exclude refractory infection or inflammation
Laboratory physician analysis states confirmation requires histopathology and immunophenotyping, which are unavailable
Pathologist analysis recommends supplementary biopsy pathology and TCR testing to verify or exclude the leading hypothesis
